title: Redwood Security BCDR / Incident Response / SLA Escalation Review - Orchid Bank
summary: Redwood team walked through incident response, RTO/RPO targets, SLA/uptime commitments and escalation procedures. Customer confirmed EU data residency requirement and asked about KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, audit logging retention and playbooks for Sev1/Sev2. Agreed to share SOC 2 Type II PDF, DR runbook, and a proposed escalation chart; pilot/test run to be scheduled within 3 weeks.
topics: BCDR: RTO & RPO targets and recovery validation
transcript:
00:00:05 - Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intro then jump into incident response and BCDR. We're here to make sure our commitments line up with Orchid's controls and compliance needs.
00:00:18 - Ayesha (Orchid): Thanks Lena, we've got Derek, Marta and Samir on. High level, we need to validate RTO/RPO, see your DR runbook, and confirm KMS options, also retention on logs.
00:00:32 - Marcus (Redwood): Great, I'll take the technical parts — architecture, how we fail over, and the escalation path. Just to set expectations, we'll cover Sev definitions and typical timelines.
00:00:45 - Derek (Orchid): Perfect. Also SOC 2 evidence — we've had some vendors give high-level answers but not the artifacts.
00:01:10 - Marcus (Redwood): Quick architecture primer: For hosted and dedicated we run a control plane plus region-local data plane. For EU residency you can enable private deployment in Frankfurt or a dedicated tenancy — data at rest remains in region; we support customer-managed KMS via bring-your-own-key across our private offering.
00:01:38 - Marta (Orchid): Is that HSM-level? Who holds keys by default?
00:01:45 - Lena (Redwood): By default Redwood manages keys, but customers can opt for BYOK with a supported KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or customer HSM via KMIP). We can provide MAA/SLA language for key ops in the Private contract.
00:02:02 - Derek (Orchid): Good. On audit logs — how long are logs retained and can we stream to our SIEM?
00:02:10 - Marcus (Redwood): Audit logs are retained 90 days by default in hosted; for enterprise we can configure 365 days or forward to customer SIEM (S3/HTTPS forwarders). There are occasional transcription artifacts where user ids are obfuscated in the UI but the raw logs include the principal. We'll include schema in the docs.
00:02:40 - Samir (Orchid): SOC 2 — do you have the Type II report and the list of controls mapped to our requirements?
00:02:47 - Lena (Redwood): Yes, we'll send the SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary, plus a control mapping spreadsheet. We'll redact vendor-specific details.
00:03:05 - Marcus (Redwood): Moving to BCDR / incident response: We use severity levels 1 through 4. Sev1 is production outage with business impact — pager within 15 minutes, 24/7 on-call escalation. Sev2 is partial degradation — initial response within 1 hour. Sev3/4 are lower priority.
00:03:25 - Derek (Orchid): And what's your RTO/RPO for Sev1?
00:03:30 - Marcus (Redwood): Our target for Sev1 on Dedicated or Private deployments is RTO 1 hour and RPO 15 minutes for critical services — that's for customers with reserved capacity. For hosted multi-tenant model the practical RTO is longer, we typically commit to fallback and mitigation; for strict RTO/RPO you should consider Dedicated or Private.
00:03:52 - Ayesha (Orchid): So for our payment flows we'd want RTO 30m if possible. Can you support that?
00:03:59 - Marcus (Redwood): We can discuss a 30-minute RTO in an elevated SLA for Dedicated capacity — it'll require runbook alignment, DR drills, and likely an on-call extension. We'll draft options.
00:04:15 - Marta (Orchid): How often do you run DR drills?
00:04:19 - Marcus (Redwood): We do quarterly tabletop exercises and annual full failovers for Dedicated customers; for Private customers we recommend at least annual together with the ops teams. We also support scheduled simulated incidents for customers to validate RPO/RTO.
00:04:35 - Derek (Orchid): Escalation path — if it's a Sev1 outside business hours who gets paged?
00:04:40 - Lena (Redwood): Pager to the on-call SE -> if not acknowledged within 15 minutes it escalates to the on-call engineering lead -> then to AE and the C-level incident contact. We'll share the escalation chart.
00:04:54 - Samir (Orchid): What about third-party dependencies — cloud provider outages?
00:04:58 - Marcus (Redwood): We have multi-AZ architecture and cross-region fallbacks. For Dedicated we can also provide cross-region replication. During cloud provider events we trigger region reroute or fall back to a compatible model variant in another region — there's a potential latency and cost impact which we document in the SLA.
00:05:20 - Ayesha (Orchid): SLA numbers?
00:05:23 - Lena (Redwood): Our standard Dedicated SLA is 99.95% monthly uptime with credits based on downtime windows. Enterprise SLAs can be negotiated to 99.99% with penalties and on-call guarantees. We'll include the SLA table in the follow-up.
00:05:40 - Derek (Orchid): How are credits calculated and what's the MTTR expectations?
00:05:43 - Marcus (Redwood): Credits tiered: e.g., < 99.95% gets 10% credit, < 99.9% gets 25% etc — we'll send the exact schedule. MTTR is incident-dependent; for Sev1 we target the 1 hour RTO for Dedicated but mean time to recovery historically is often within 45–90 minutes depending on the root cause.
00:06:08 - Marta (Orchid): Can we see past incident postmortems or a summary?
00:06:12 - Lena (Redwood): We can share redacted postmortems for incidents that affected customers and a summary of corrective actions; there is an NDA requirement for detailed docs.
00:06:28 - Marcus (Redwood): Onboarding and playbooks: we provide runbooks for common failure modes — model OOM, KV cache corruption, control plane network partition. The runbooks include remediation steps, rollback commands, and verification checks.
00:06:45 - Derek (Orchid): KV cache — sometimes docs say KC cache, just to note we've seen name confusion in earlier vendors.
00:06:52 - Marcus (Redwood): Ha, yeah sometimes transcription spells KV as KC. It's key-value cache for auto-unroll.
00:07:02 - Ayesha (Orchid): For encryption in transit and at rest — TLS plus envelope encryption?
00:07:08 - Marcus (Redwood): TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, envelope encryption at rest with customer-managed keys if requested. For Private we support HSM-backed keys. We can show the KMS integration diagram.
00:07:22 - Samir (Orchid): SSO & RBAC — do you support SAML + SCIM?
00:07:27 - Lena (Redwood): Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, plus granular RBAC roles (admin, dev, observer, billing). We can map to your existing AD groups.
00:07:40 - Marta (Orchid): Audit log format — do you store logs in immutable storage and what's the tamper-evidence?
00:07:46 - Marcus (Redwood): Audit logs are write-once in our retention store with checksums; we can provide integrity proofs and forward logs to your SIEM for redundancy.
00:08:00 - Derek (Orchid): For incident notification — do you do post-incident reports within a set SLA?
00:08:05 - Lena (Redwood): For Sev1 we aim to produce a preliminary incident report within 48 hours and a full postmortem within 10 business days.
00:08:15 - Ayesha (Orchid): Who owns the communication with regulators if data residency or PII is at risk?
00:08:20 - Marcus (Redwood): We coordinate with the customer; Redwood will provide technical details and assist with forensic data, but the customer maintains ownership for external regulator communications. We'll provide a template to help with notifications.
00:08:40 - Samir (Orchid): Can you enforce data residency for backups as well?
00:08:45 - Marcus (Redwood): Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can ensure backups are stored in-region. For hosted customers we offer region-scoped backups but recommend Dedicated if you require strict residency for backups.
00:09:02 - Lena (Redwood): Quick pause — any blockers at this point?
00:09:06 - Derek (Orchid): Main blockers: we need SOC2 Type II, KMS BYOK proof, runbook examples, and clarity on RTO 30m option. Also need escalation contacts.
00:09:18 - Lena (Redwood): We'll provide those. Next, sample incident scenario walkthrough?
00:09:23 - Ayesha (Orchid): Yes, walk through a payment ingestion outage — step through roles and timeline.
00:09:30 - Marcus (Redwood): Scenario: Model serving cluster experiences OOM and KV cache corruption causing 100% error rate for payment route. Detection: synthetic monitors and customer health checks detect spike. Initial detection -> pager to on-call SE at T+0. Investigation T+5 minutes -> rollback model or spin new node pool, restore cache from latest checkpoint (RPO 15m). If no ack, escalate. We'll annotate timelines: T+15 escalate to lead, T+30 mitigation plan, T+60 restore for Dedicated target.
00:10:10 - Marta (Orchid): Who does the cache restore — Redwood ops or our infra?
00:10:14 - Marcus (Redwood): Redwood will perform restore for hosted/dedicated. For Private we help coordinate and can provide runbook steps for your team to run.
00:10:25 - Derek (Orchid): How do you validate completeness after restore?
00:10:29 - Marcus (Redwood): We run smoke checks, end-to-end sample requests, and compare counters. We'll include the verification checklist in the runbook.
00:10:45 - Ayesha (Orchid): Can we automate the failover to a read-only fallback mode while recovery occurs?
00:10:50 - Marcus (Redwood): Yes, policy-based routing can send traffic to a stable model variant or a degra ded mode; that costs more tokens but keeps latency predictable.
00:11:05 - Samir (Orchid): Regarding legal — if there's a breach, what's your liability cap and notification SLA?
00:11:11 - Lena (Redwood): That's in the contract — standard liability cap tied to subscription fees, and breach notification within 72 hours of confirmation per GDPR; we can surface the specific clause for review.
00:11:27 - Derek (Orchid): Do you have a SOC 2 subservice org matrix?
00:11:31 - Lena (Redwood): Yes, we'll include the subservice org list and the relevant provider attestations.
00:11:45 - Marcus (Redwood): A couple of practical items: for the 30-minute RTO option we'll need a runbook alignment session and at least two dry runs. That tends to uncover environment-specific gaps.
00:11:58 - Ayesha (Orchid): Sounds fair. Timeline — can we get the docs this week and schedule a DR run in three weeks?
00:12:05 - Lena (Redwood): Yes, we'll send SOC2, DR runbook, escalation chart and proposed SLA amendments by Friday. We'll also propose a DR slot in three weeks.
00:12:18 - Marta (Orchid): For monitoring access, can we get read-only dashboards in your console scoped to our account?
00:12:24 - Lena (Redwood): Yes, read-only dashboards via RBAC. We'll provision SCIM groups and a dedicated observer role.
00:12:35 - Derek (Orchid): One last thing — audit log retention for forensic analysis: we may request 2 years of retention for specific audit logs. Can that be accommodated?
00:12:44 - Marcus (Redwood): We can extend to 2 years for an enterprise add-on; logs forwarded to your S3 bucket provide indefinite retention on your side.
00:12:55 - Samir (Orchid): Okay great.
00:13:00 - Lena (Redwood): We'll capture action items now and recap.
00:13:05 - Marcus (Redwood): Thanks everyone.

[End of recorded transcript excerpt — remaining portion was discussion scheduling and confirmations, ~34 minutes in total follow-up Q&A and contractual clarifications not fully transcribed due to meeting notes truncation. Some speaker labels auto-generated and may have slight attribution errors.]
